issues.t: Clogged PCV oil trap causes leaks and whistling
issues.sym: A whistle or squeal at idle that stops when you remove the oil cap, oil leaks from seals, a rough idle, a check engine light, the dipstick popping up, or higher oil use.
issues.why: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) oil trap, which is built into the oil filter housing on these cars, and its hoses clog with sludge. Pressure then builds inside the engine and pushes oil past seals. Short trips and long oil-change intervals make it worse.
issues.next: Have the PCV system checked and the oil trap and hoses replaced; Volvo suggests doing it around 100,000 miles. Don't ignore it, because blown seals are a much bigger repair.

issues.t: Fuel pressure sensor failure
issues.sym: A check engine light, hesitation, rough running, hard starting or stalling.
issues.why: The fuel pressure sensor on the fuel rail fails and gives the engine computer wrong readings. It is one of the more common repairs owners report.
issues.next: Have the codes read. The sensor is a fairly quick replacement.

issues.t: Noisy front or rear wheel bearings
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that rises with speed and may change when turning.
issues.why: Wheel bearings and hubs are the most reported repair on the S40, often failing between 40,000 and 150,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the noisy corner identified and the hub bearing replaced. A failing bearing can get loose and affect braking and steering.

issues.t: Worn struts and strut mounts
issues.sym: A bouncy ride, knocking over bumps, leaking struts, or clicking from the front when turning.
issues.why: Struts and their top mounts are among the most common S40 repairs.
issues.next: Have the struts and mounts checked and replace them in pairs.

issues.t: Torn CV boots and worn axles
issues.sym: Clicking when turning, vibration when accelerating, or grease spattered inside the wheel.
issues.why: CV axle boots tear and let grit into the joint, which then wears out.
issues.next: Replace a torn boot early, or the whole axle if it already clicks.

issues.t: Worn engine mounts cause vibration
issues.sym: More vibration at idle or in gear and a clunk when accelerating.
issues.why: The engine and torque mounts wear or leak their fluid.
issues.next: Have the mounts inspected and replace any that are torn.

issues.t: Sunroof drains clog and leak water inside
issues.sym: Wet carpets in the footwells or under the seats, a musty smell, foggy windows, or electrical problems after rain.
issues.why: The sunroof drain tubes clog or come loose. Water then runs into the cabin and can damage wiring and modules under the seats.
issues.next: Clear the drains, dry the carpets fully, and check the wiring under the seats for corrosion.

issues.t: A/C compressor or clutch failure
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm, cuts out after 10–20 minutes, or the compressor won't engage.
issues.why: The A/C compressor and its clutch wear out; the clutch often fails first.
issues.next: Have the system tested before recharging. A clutch or shim repair may save replacing the whole compressor.

issues.t: Alternator fails and drains the battery
issues.sym: Battery warning light, dim lights, or the car dying or not starting.
issues.why: Alternators fail at moderate mileage on these cars.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested before replacing the battery.

issues.t: Central electronic module (CEM) faults
issues.sym: Wipers that won't turn off, a wrong fuel gauge, random warning lights, locks or windows misbehaving, or a no-start.
issues.why: The CEM controls most body electronics. Water leaks and corroded connections are the main causes, and a weak battery can mimic it.
issues.next: Check the battery, grounds and any water leaks first. A specialist can repair or reprogram the module.

issues.t: Transmission Service Urgent message or harsh shifting
issues.sym: A 'Transmission Service Urgent' message, bucking, slipping or odd shifts.
issues.why: The automatic transmission's control software and internals cause shift complaints; dealer software updates fixed many cases, but some transmissions failed.
issues.next: Ask a Volvo dealer about transmission software updates first, and check the fluid. A full replacement is the last resort.

issues.t: Coolant expansion tank cracks
issues.sym: Coolant loss, a sweet smell, low coolant warning or overheating.
issues.why: The plastic coolant reservoir can crack and leak all its coolant.
issues.next: Replace the tank and refill with the correct coolant. Stop driving if it overheats.

issues.t: Clogged PCV flame trap pushes out seals
issues.sym: Oil leaks around the camshaft seals or front of the engine, oil in the intake, or oil smoke.
issues.why: The PCV system and the ports in the engine block clog, pressure builds in the crankcase and pushes seals out.
issues.next: Replace the PCV box and hoses, clean the block ports, then fix any seal that still leaks.
issues.sevReason: Rule false positive: "flame trap" is the PCV part name; the problem is an oil leak, not a fire.

issues.t: Broken front coil springs
issues.sym: A clunk or scraping noise, the car sitting lower on one corner, or a sagging front end.
issues.why: The coil springs on these cars can snap, often at the bottom coil.
issues.next: Have the car inspected right away; a broken spring can damage the tire or strut. Replace springs in pairs.

issues.t: Radiator leak can ruin the transmission
issues.sym: Coolant loss, a low coolant level, or slipping transmission shifts.
issues.why: Radiators corrode and leak at the end caps, and hoses leak. On automatic cars the transmission cooler is inside the radiator, so a leak can let coolant into the transmission fluid and destroy it.
issues.next: Fix coolant leaks quickly. If the transmission starts slipping, have the fluid checked for coolant contamination.

issues.t: Heater fan only works on some speeds
issues.sym: The blower fan only works on high, some speeds don't work, or it stops altogether.
issues.why: The blower resistor fails. A 2001 recall also replaced a climate control diode that could wear out early.
issues.next: Have the resistor and fan motor tested; the resistor is a simple part.

issues.t: Worn sway bar links and bushings
issues.sym: Knocking or rattling over bumps and notchy or loose steering.
issues.why: Stabilizer bar end links and bushings wear out on both generations.
issues.next: Have the front end checked. Links are quick to replace.

issues.t: Brake vacuum pump failure makes the pedal hard (recall)
issues.sym: A hard brake pedal, longer stopping distances, especially in cold weather, and sometimes an ABS warning.
issues.why: The electric brake vacuum pump can fail or blow its fuse, removing power assist. NHTSA investigated and Volvo recalled the pump (recall 03V-474).
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. A hard brake pedal means the brake assist has failed, so the car needs much more force and distance to stop. If it happens while driving, press the pedal firmly, slow down and pull off the road when it's safe. Don't keep driving it: have it towed to a dealer. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Engine revs up or surges on its own
issues.sym: Engine speed jumps to 3,000 RPM or more, the car lurches or pulls when stopped, or it surges forward.
issues.why: Owners filed many complaints. Shops replaced the coolant temperature sensor, idle air valve, throttle and airflow sensor with mixed results; no single cause was confirmed.
issues.next: Shift to neutral and brake firmly if it happens. Have the throttle, idle control and temperature sensor tested by a Volvo specialist.

issues.t: Fuel rail can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell in the engine bay.
issues.why: Poor welding can let the fuel rail leak, creating a fire risk (recall 03V-424).
issues.next: Check your VIN; the dealer adds a clamp for free.

issues.t: Brake booster vacuum check valve can crack (recall)
issues.sym: A harder brake pedal and rough idle.
issues.why: A poorly welded check valve in the brake vacuum hose can crack (recall 04V-493).
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check your VIN; the dealer replaces the hose for free.

issues.t: Brake master cylinder seal can leak (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal needs more effort and braking gradually weakens.
issues.why: A soft coating in the master cylinder can wear a seal and leak fluid internally (recall 08V-101).
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Check your VIN; the dealer replaces the master cylinder for free.

issues.t: Manual gearshift can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Gears are hard or impossible to select on 6-speed manual cars.
issues.why: The gearshift lever stud may not have been tightened properly (recall 10V-255).
issues.next: Check your VIN; the dealer tightens it for free.

issues.t: Passenger seat can slide too far forward (recall)
issues.sym: The front passenger seat moves farther forward than it should.
issues.why: The seat rail end-stop detection was made wrong (recall 10V-591).
issues.next: Check your VIN; the dealer repairs the rails for free.

issues.t: Front structure support member may be cracked (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms; crash protection may be reduced.
issues.why: A support member in the engine bay could crack during manufacturing (recall 11V-186).
issues.next: Check your VIN; affected cars were inspected and replaced if cracked.
